newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Refugees return to Zaire camps, witnesses say.
newsitem.headline: Refugees return to Zaire camps, witnesses say.

text.p: Thousands of Rwandan Hutu refugees returned on Monday to camps south of the Zairean city of Kisangani they fled last week, while dozens of compatriots who died in the exodus lay unburied, witnesses said.
Aid officials and journalists who manged to visit Biaro camp, 41 (25 miles) south of Kisangani city, saw about 5,000 refugees drifting out of the forest back to their camps.
More than 30 corpses lay at three sites surrounding the makeshift hospital at the camp. Aid officials said some had died of illness but others had clearly been butchered and had savage wounds.

It was the first time aid officials had been able to travel to Biaro for over a week. Zairean rebel leader Laurent Kabila gave the United Nations 60 days to repatriate up to 100,000 refugees who fled sites south of Kisangani last week.

But Kabila's promise to allow aid officials full access to all areas under rebel control came up against its first hurdle as rebel soldiers refused to allow an aid convoy to travel further south than Biaro.

"I am very disappointed we cannot go further," said Aldo Ajello, European Union special envoy to the Great Lakes region, who was in the convoy. "We have been promised full access but it seems not to be the case."
